text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's foreign trade deficit for 1996 is expected to exceed 50 billion crowns, the economics ministry said.

- Slovakia's M2 money reserves stood at 378 billion crowns as of the end of September, 1.5 billion crowns more than in the previous month, Vladimir Masar, Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said.
- The recently approved securities law affects not only small investors, but will also call for a revision of the NBS stock market control mechanism, Masar said.

- Slovakia's farmers made a loss of 3.4 billion crowns in the first half of this year, an 8.8 percent increase over the same period last year. Overall productivity measured in terms of value-added volume was almost 16 percent lower in the first six months of this year.
NARODNA OBRODDA - Slovakia's sole electric power producer Slovenske Elektrarne is pushing for an annual increase in energy prices in the range of five to seven percent over inflation.
- Slovakia's annual consumer price inflation figure for 1996 should stand at around six percent, NBS chief Masar said.

- The Constitutional Court rejected an appeal by President Michal Kovac against parliament's decision to relieve him of the power to appoint the head of the secret service, the SIS. But the court upheld his right to appoint the chief of the army general staff.

SME - The National Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, in its budget for next year, plans incomes totalling 15.9 billion crowns, of which 4.7 billion will be in cash and the rest in bonds. Sales of state enterprises are to result in an income of 3.9 billion crowns.

- The number of suicides in Slovakia has increased over the past few years. According to official statistics there were 500 suicides in Slovakia last year, but some experts and psychiatrists put the figures much higher. Four times more men commit suicide than women.
SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar will attend a two-day summit of the Central European Initiative in Graz, Austria. He will be accompanied by foreign minister Pavol Hamzik.

- Frantisek Gaulieder, the parliamentarian from the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), who quit the HZDS parliamentary club earlier this week, has in no way damaged the unity of the club and there will be no further defections.

PRAVDA - Slovakia will have to import about one fifth of its electricity needs next year due to to a fall in domestic production as a result of reconstruction work and the upgrading of Slovakia's power plants.
